resources.string: A few steps, and you can translate text, photos and other apps. You can change every option later.
Use text and photos for now
Choose the language you read and a translation service. Google works without a key. For MyMemory and offline translation, choose a specific source language.
Open Android settings, find Click’n’Translate and enable “Display over other apps”. Return here; the status updates automatically.
Allow notifications to see the running translator, stop capture and follow model downloads. Translation can also work without this permission.
Android will ask for screen sharing when you start translation. On Android 14+, choose the entire screen to translate across apps. You can stop capture at any time.

On Android 11+, enable the Click’n’Translate accessibility service for screenshots without repeated screen-sharing prompts. It also supports volume-key shortcuts and input translation. Only enable it if you want these features. If Android 13 or later blocks this switch, open App info, then the three-dot menu and Allow restricted settings. Return here to enable the service.
The default OCR recognizes Latin, Chinese, Japanese and Korean scripts. For Cyrillic or other scripts, select a suitable OCR service. Offline translation models must be downloaded before use.
If your phone stops the overlay in the background, allow background activity or remove battery restrictions for Click’n’Translate. Android settings vary by device.
On the Screen tab, tap Start and confirm screen sharing. Open another app and use the floating CT button to select a region. Text and photo translation are available without screen capture.
Your phone did not open that setting. Open Android settings and find Click’n’Translate manually.
